# Nomad Echo Sounds

> Real field recordings of mountain water from the Ile Alatau (Northern Tian Shan, near Almaty, Kazakhstan). Every recording is measured for loudness steadiness, sudden peaks and tone drift before it becomes a long track for sleep and tinnitus masking. No AI-generated audio. Recorded on a Zoom H5, WAV 48 kHz / 24-bit.

## Guides
- [Which natural sounds mask tinnitus best?](https://nomadechosounds.com/tinnitus-masking-sounds/): Measurements of real recordings (loudness variation, P95–P5 spread, transient counts, spectral centroid); which passed and why; preparation chain; research references.
- [How to use a masking sound at night](https://nomadechosounds.com/how-to-use-masking-sounds-at-night/): Volume a little below the tinnitus, speaker vs pillow speaker vs headphones, timer vs all night, steady sounds; summarises Tinnitus UK and NHS advice with our measurements (L/R balance, drift, loop seam). FAQ.
- [Is birdsong good for sleep?](https://nomadechosounds.com/birdsong-for-sleep/): A dawn birdsong recording measured against a mountain brook: 42 loud events per minute vs none, 3.73 dB vs 0.31 dB loudness variation.
- [Tian Shan field recordings](https://nomadechosounds.com/tian-shan-field-recordings/): Where and how the recordings are made: Ile Alatau, about 1,500 m, spring 2026, equipment and spot selection.
- [Mountain Brook: recording notes](https://nomadechosounds.com/recordings/mountain-brook/): Full measurements of our steadiest Tian Shan brook recording (0.31 dB loudness variation, no peaks >6 dB), the 3.5 dB channel imbalance fix and the preparation chain.
- [Mountain River: recording notes](https://nomadechosounds.com/recordings/mountain-river/): Measurements of a loud but constant Tian Shan river over 20 minutes (0.62 dB loudness variation, no peaks >10 dB, 0.6 dB drift), comparison with the brook and the preparation chain.
- [How we record water sounds](https://nomadechosounds.com/how-we-record-water-sounds/): Our field setup: Zoom H5 with a fur windscreen, WAV 48 kHz / 24-bit, recorder a little back from the water (in the shallows at Kapchagay), takes of 20+ minutes on weekdays, recording level example, every take measured.

## Data
- [How steady are nature sounds? Measurement data](https://nomadechosounds.com/nature-sound-measurements/): One table of all measured recordings (loudness variation, P95–P5 spread, sudden peaks, spectral centroid, drift, sub-40 Hz energy, L/R balance), method, limits, CSV download (CC BY 4.0, numbers only).

## About
- [About Nomad Echo Sounds](https://nomadechosounds.com/about/): Who records these sounds, how they are measured, and how the site is written.
- [AI Data Services](https://nomadechosounds.com/ai-data-collection/): A developing B2B service: collection of real-world audio, video, photo and regional language material in Kazakhstan and Central Asia for AI training. Scope agreed per project; contributor network being formed.

## Listen
- [Nature sound library](https://nomadechosounds.com/library/): Every long-form recording, grouped by sound, playable on the page.
- [YouTube channel: Nomad Echo ASMR](https://www.youtube.com/@NomadEchoASMR): Long black-screen tinnitus relief and sleep tracks made from these recordings.

## Notes
- Content is for relaxation and general information, not medical advice.
